items.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995
items.q: I remember the first time I went to his home I walked in and there was a picture of the Blue Boy with Spike’s head on top of it

ctx.x: Yeah, you had to be good to play in that.

And everything was timed to the second. And there was no goofing on that gig, believe me. Spike was a funny man but he was a taskmaster too, you know, you had to do it. I remember the first time I went to his home I walked in and there was a picture of the Blue Boy with Spike’s head on top of it, which cracked me up. But then the next picture was Whistler’s Mother with a racing form in her lap. And that was Spike all the way. He used to go to all the dog kennels when we were traveling, and tape the dogs barking…
